zajjaj:1-2.t:
Sūrat al-Muzzammil
Meccan, except for two verses at its end, which are Medinan
﷽
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها المُزَّمِّلُ﴾ ﴿قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾ ("O you wrapped in garments, stand [in prayer] the night, except a little"): this is an address to the Prophet (peace be upon him). It was said that this was revealed to him while a velvet wrap was over him. «المُزَّمِّل» is originally «المُتَزَمِّل», but the tāʾ is assimilated into the zāy because of its closeness to it. One says «تَزَمَّلَ فُلانٌ» when someone wraps himself in his clothes, and everything wrapped has been «زُمِّلَ». Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎كَأنَّ أبانًا في أفانِينِ ودْقِهِ ∗∗∗ كَبِيرُ أُناسٍ في بِجادٍ مُزَمَّلِ
(As though [Mount] Abān, amid the varied sheets of its downpour, were a chief of men wrapped in a striped cloak.)
And it was said that he was wrapped up in the attire of prayer.
His saying: ﴿قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إلا قَلِيلا﴾ ﴿نِصْفَهُ أوِ انْقُصْ مِنهُ قَلِيلا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3] ﴿أوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4] ("Stand the night, except a little — half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it"): the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that «نِصْفَهُ» is a badal (substitute) for «اللَّيْلَ», as you say «ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا رَأْسَهُ» ("I struck Zayd, his head"): you mentioned «زَيْدًا» only to emphasise the statement, and it is more emphatic than your saying «ضَرَبْتُ رَأْسَ زَيْدٍ» ("I struck Zayd's head"). So the meaning is: "Stand half the night except a little, or subtract from the half, or add to the half." He mentioned ﴿أوِ انْقُصْ مِنهُ قَلِيلا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3] in the meaning of «إلّا قَلِيلًا», but it was mentioned together with the addition; so the meaning is: "Stand half the night, or subtract from half the night, or add to a half." This — and Allah knows best — was before the obligation of the five prayers came.
The meaning of ﴿وَرَتِّلِ القُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4] ("and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation") is: make it clear distinctly. Clarity is not achieved by hurrying through the Qur'an; it is achieved only by making all the letters clear and giving them their full due in fullness of pronunciation.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿واصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ واهْجُرْهم هَجْرًا جَمِيلا﴾ ("And be patient over what they say and avoid them with gracious avoidance"): this indicates — and Allah knows best — [that it was] before the Muslims were commanded to fight.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
﴿وَذَرْنِي والمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ ومَهِّلْهم قَلِيلا﴾ ("And leave Me with the deniers, the possessors of ease, and give them respite a little"); and similar to it is ﴿ذَرْنِي ومَن خَلَقْتُ وحِيدًا﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11] ("Leave Me with the one I created alone").
If someone says: what is the sense of «ذَرْنِي» ("leave Me"), when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does whatever He wills, and no barrier stands between Him and His will? The answer to that is that when the Arabs want to tell a person that they are intent upon some matter or some person, they say «دَعْنِي وزَيْدًا» ("leave me and Zayd") — not that anyone is standing between him and Zayd; rather its interpretation is: "Do not concern yourself with Zayd, for I shall deal with him for you."

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ لَدَيْنا أنْكالا وجَحِيمًا﴾ ("Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire"): the singular of «الأنْكال» is «نِكْل», and it has come in the exegesis that here it means fetters of fire.
﴿وَطَعامًا ذا غُصَّةٍ وعَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 13] ("and food that chokes, and a painful punishment"): their food is ḍarīʿ, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهم طَعامٌ إلا مِن ضَرِيعٍ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 6] ("They will have no food except from ḍarīʿ"); it is shibriq, a thorny plant like boxthorn.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الأرْضُ والجِبالُ وكانَتِ الجِبالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلا﴾ ("On the Day the earth and the mountains will convulse, and the mountains will become a heap of sand pouring down"): «يَوْمَ» is accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying ﴿إنَّ لَدَيْنا أنْكالا وجَحِيمًا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 12] ("Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing Fire"), i.e. "the unbelievers will be made an example of, and He will punish them, on the Day the earth and the mountains convulse." «تَرْجُفُ» means: it will be shaken and moved with the most violent movement.
﴿وَكانَتِ الجِبالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلا﴾: the plural of «الكَثِيب» is «الكُثْبان», which are great masses of sand. The meaning of ﴿مَهِيلا﴾ is flowing, made to pour. The original of «مَهِيل» is «مَهْيُول»; one says «تُرابٌ مَهِيلٌ» and «تُرابٌ مَهْيُولٌ», i.e. poured out, made to flow, and «مَهِيل» is more common. The wāw was dropped only because the ḍamma is removed from the yāʾ in «مَهْيُول», so it and the wāw are quiescent, and the wāw is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. We have explained this in a similar place at greater length than this explanation, and we have kept it brief here in view of what preceded, because the grammarians disagree about it and its explanation would be long in this book.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿فَأخَذْناهُ أخْذًا وبِيلا﴾ ("So We seized him with a ruinous seizure"): «الوَبِيل» is the very heavy and severe; from this, heavy, great rain is called «وابِل».

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الوِلْدانَ شِيبًا﴾ ("Then how can you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve, against a Day that will make children white-haired?"): the meaning is "How can you guard yourselves against a Day that will make children white-haired, if you disbelieve", i.e. by what will you be protected from Allah's punishment on a Day from whose terror the young turn grey without old age, every nursing mother forgets what she nursed, and you see people drunk though they are not drunk — but the punishment of Allah is severe. Then He described, of the terror of that Day, that He said: ﴿السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18] ("the sky will be split thereby"), i.e. the sky will be split open by it, as He said: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 1] ("When the sky is split open"). And it was said in the exegesis: ﴿السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 18], i.e. the sky will be weighed down by Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ﴾ ("split thereby"), and He did not say «مُنْفَطِرَةٌ» — though «مُنْفَطِرَةٌ» is permissible, and on that came ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْفَطَرَتْ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 1] ("When the sky breaks apart"); but it is not permissible to read in this place «السَّماءُ مُنْفَطِرَةٌ», because it contradicts the Muṣḥaf. The masculine is on two lines. One of them is on the meaning that «السَّماء» means the roof; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا السَّماءَ سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 32] ("And We made the sky a protected roof"). The second line is on [the model of] the saying «اِمْرَأةٌ مُرْضِعٌ» ("a suckling woman"), i.e. by way of attribution (nasab): the meaning is "the sky, possessed of splitting", as you say «اِمْرَأةٌ مُرْضِعٌ», i.e. "possessed of suckling".
And His saying: ﴿أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 11] ("possessors of ease"): «النَّعْمَة» is luxurious living, and «النِّعْمَة» is the kindly favour done to a person, and the beneficence of Allah the Exalted. Had it been read «أُولِي النِّعْمَةِ», it would have been a valid line, because those on whom favour is bestowed may be believers or non-believers; Allah, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿صِراطَ الَّذِينَ أنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [al-Fātiḥa: 7] ("the path of those You have favoured, not of those who incurred wrath").
[Translator's note: the source writes both words as «اَلنَّعْمَةُ»; the second, glossed as "favour", is evidently «النِّعْمَة» with kasra and is rendered so.]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَما تُقَدِّمُوا لأنْفُسِكم مِن خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ هو خَيْرًا وأعْظَمَ أجْرًا﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20] ("And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward"): its meaning is "better for you than the enjoyment of this world". «خَيْرًا» is accusative, the second mafʿūl (object) of «تَجِدُوهُ», and «هُوَ» came in as a separating pronoun (faṣl). We have explained that earlier in the book. Had it been outside the Qur'an, «تَجِدُوهُ هو خَيْرٌ» would be permissible, so that you would make it nominative with «هُوَ» [as mubtadaʾ]; but the accusative is better in Arabic, and nothing else is permissible in the Qur'an.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أنَّكَ تَقُومُ أدْنى مِن ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ ونِصْفَهُ وثُلُثَهُ﴾ ("Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] nearly two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it"). Whoever reads ﴿نِصْفَهُ﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3] in the accusative, and ﴿وَثُلُثَهُ﴾, it is clear and good: it is an explanation of the measure of his standing, because when He said ﴿أدْنى مِن ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ﴾ ("nearly two-thirds of the night"), "half of it" was an explanation of that "nearly". Whoever reads «وَنِصْفِهِ وثُلُثِهِ» (genitive), the meaning is: "and you stand less than half of it and than a third of it."

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلا ثَقِيلا﴾ ("Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word"). It has come in the exegesis that acting upon it is heavy, because the lawful and the unlawful, prayer and fasting, and everything Allah has commanded to be done and has forbidden — no one carries it out except by undertaking what is heavy for him. And it is possible, according to the doctrine of the lexicographers, that its meaning is that it is a word that has weight in its soundness, its clarity and its benefit, as you say «هَذا كَلامٌ رَصِينٌ» ("this is weighty speech") and «هَذا قَوْلٌ لَهُ وزْنٌ» ("this is a statement that has weight") when you consider it excellent and know that it has hit the mark of wisdom and clarity.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ ناشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هي أشَدُّ وطْئًا﴾ ("Indeed, the rising by night is firmer in waṭʾ") — and it is read «وَطاءً» — ﴿وَأقْوَمُ قِيلا﴾ ("and more upright in speech"). «ناشِئَةُ اللَّيْلِ» are all the hours of the night, whenever any of it arises; i.e. everything that occurs of it is a nāshiʾa. The meaning of «هِيَ أشَدُّ وطْئًا» is: it is more in harmony (muwāṭaʾa) with the turning of the hearing. Whoever reads ﴿وَطْئًا﴾ with fatḥa on the wāw, its meaning is: it is more effective in standing [in prayer] and clearer in speech. It is possible that «أشَدُّ وطْئًا» means: heavier upon a person than standing by day, because the night was made for rest. And it was said: «أشَدُّ وطْئًا», i.e. greater in reward, because the reward of everyone who strives is in proportion to his striving.
[Translator's note: «لِتَقَلُّبِ السَّمْعِ» ("the turning of the hearing") may be a corruption of «لِلْقَلْبِ والسَّمْعِ» ("the heart and the hearing"). Also, the text says the reading with fatḥa on the wāw (waṭʾan) gives the second sense; the variant mentioned earlier is «وِطاءً», so the vowelling may be disturbed. Both translated as written.]

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ لَكَ في النَّهارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلا﴾ ("Indeed, for you by day is prolonged occupation") means: long free time and long scope for going about.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿واذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾ ("And remember the name of your Lord"), i.e. if you miss anything of the night, you have free time in the day.
It was also read «سَبْخًا» with the dotted khāʾ, while the [established] reading is with the undotted ḥāʾ. The meaning of «سَبْخًا» is sound in the language: a piece of cotton is called «سَبْخَة», and one says «سَبَخْتُ القُطْنَ» meaning «نَفَشْتُهُ» ("I teased the cotton out"), and the meaning of «نَفَشْتُهُ» is "I spread it out". So the meaning on that basis is: "Indeed, for you by day is long room for ease", and its meaning is close to the meaning of «السَّبْح».
﴿واذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وتَبَتَّلْ إلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلا﴾ ("And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion"): the meaning is "remember the name of your Lord by day". The meaning of ﴿وَتَبَتَّلْ إلَيْهِ﴾ is: cut yourself off [from all else] to Him in worship. From this Mary (peace be upon her) was called «البَتُول», because she cut herself off to Allah, exalted be His praise, in worship; and likewise «صَدَقَةٌ بَتْلَةٌ» is an alms cut off from the property of the almsgiver and going out to the ways of Allah. The original form of the maṣdar of «تَبَتَّلَ» is «تَبَتَّلْتُ تَبَتُّلًا», and «بَتَّلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا»; so «تَبْتِيلًا» is construed according to the meaning of "devote yourself to Him with complete devotion".
[Translator's note: the source prints «تَبَتَّلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا» and «بَتِلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا»; the argument requires «تَبَتَّلْتُ تَبَتُّلًا» and «بَتَّلْتُ تَبْتِيلًا», which is how it is rendered above.]

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فاتَّخِذْهُ وكِيلا﴾ ("so take Him as Disposer of affairs"), i.e. take Him as guarantor of what He has promised you.
